Subject: Private VPC: narrow-window version pinning & rollback cadence

Hi team,

Per our call last week, Acme is asking for a tight, low-impact maintenance approach for the upcoming Private deployment patch (minor runtime + security fixes). The ask: a short, auditable maintenance window where we can unpin/pin a specific agent build and, if needed, roll back quickly to the previous pin with minimal customer impact.

Key constraints Acme called out:
- Must avoid >5% error spike and no >250ms p99 latency regression for production tenants during the window.
- SOC2 evidence for changes and an audit trail of pins/rollbacks.
- Prefer a single 60-90 minute window that impacts only the pinned worker set.

My proposal (attached: Acme_PinMatrix_v1.xlsx + vpc-network-diagram.pdf):
1) Narrow maintenance window: 60 minutes, preflight health checks 20m, cutover 25m, validation 15m.
2) Pin policy: pin at cluster-level, keep previous pin in escrow for 72 hours.
3) Canary: 2 node canary in each AZ for 15m with KV cache warm-up.
4) Rollback triggers: >3% error rate increase OR sustained p99 >250ms for 5m OR failing critical e2e smoke tests.
5) Evidence: auto-capture of pin events to the audit log + signed change log (ops-runbook-v1.md will cover procedure).

Ask: confirm owners and availability for proposed windows below (I included two tentative slots). Also need Acme Ops to confirm blackout windows and whether they require an extended pin escrow (>72h).

Proposed windows (PST):
- Option A: Fri, 2026-07-23 02:00-03:00
- Option B: Tue, 2026-07-27 22:00-23:00

Action owners I propose:
- Karthik: preflight canary tests + rollback script validation
- Marissa: runbook lead and communications
- Olga: network gate & ACL preflight verification
- Jonas: post-change telemetry checks and SLA guard

Thanks — I want to lock this by EOD Wed so we can schedule the dry-run.

--

Subject: Re: Private VPC: narrow-window version pinning & rollback cadence

Neha — thanks, this is a good start. A few technical notes from the runtime side before we lock windows: 

- KV cache warm-up: 15m per canary is fine, but cold-starts for quantized kernels can add ~30-90s per model shard. We'll need to ensure the canary covers the heaviest shard and that the cache is pre-populated with a representative prefix set.
- Pin semantics: pin at the deployment unit (pool) rather than binary-level to avoid inconsistent kernel selection. We should capture the model hash + quantization profile in the audit event.
- Rollback automation: I propose a two-step rollback script: 1) atomic pin swap + immediate traffic redirect to previous pool, 2) KV flush to avoid stale state. The script is in PROJ-1234 (https://jira.redwood.com/browse/PROJ-1234).
- Safety net: if rollback is triggered, we should have an automatic cold-shed of low-priority queues for 10 minutes to reduce pressure while the previous pin warms up.

Risks to call out to Acme: if a patch changes sampling/attention configs, we may see initial quality regressions on long-sequence workloads that don't surface in short e2e smoke tests. Recommend we include 5 production prompts (provided by Acme) as part of the validation set.

I can lead the preflight canary automation and run the rollback script validation on the dry-run.

- SLA impact: for a single-cluster pin, expected customer downtime risk is very low; we'll keep status pages in read-only mode for the pinned tenant set.
- Rollback ownership: ops will run the rollback script but need a clear abort signal owner. Recommend Jonas as primary abort authority (he has access to telemetry dashboards).
- Dry-run: ops wants to run a dry-run on 2026-07-20 at 02:30 for 45 minutes (non-prod mirror). This will validate the pre-stage + canary warm-up.
